final_codebook.domain: Subtraction of fractions, mixed numbers, and whole numbers with simplification

skills.name: Equalize denominators
skills.definition: Find a common denominator and rewrite one or more fraction parts as equivalent fractions so the fractional units match before subtraction.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a step explicitly finds an LCD or common denominator.
Tag when one or both fractions are converted to equivalent fractions with a shared denominator before subtraction.
Tag in mixed-number items when only the fractional parts are equalized.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when denominators already match and no equivalent-fraction conversion is performed.
Do not tag rewriting a whole number as a whole plus 0 over a denominator unless the step's main purpose is denominator equalization.
Do not tag simplification after subtraction.

skills.name: Normalize number form
skills.definition: Rewrite a whole number, mixed number, or nonstandard mixed number into a compatible whole-and-fraction structure for subtraction.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a whole number is rewritten as a whole plus 0 over a denominator.
Tag when a mixed number with an improper fraction part is normalized to a standard mixed number.
Tag when a mixed number is explicitly decomposed or separated into whole and fractional parts to set up componentwise subtraction.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag ordinary subtraction when the quantities are already in workable form and no structural rewrite occurs.
Do not tag borrowing or regrouping after subtraction has begun.
Do not tag common-denominator conversion unless the step also performs a structural rewrite of the number form.

skills.name: Subtract aligned parts
skills.definition: Perform the subtraction once quantities are in compatible form by subtracting like fractions and/or subtracting whole and fractional parts separately.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when like-denominator fractions are subtracted directly by subtracting numerators.
Tag when whole parts and fraction parts of mixed numbers are subtracted separately.
Tag when a step carries out the actual subtraction even if it produces a zero or negative fractional difference before any regrouping.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag steps whose main purpose is finding a common denominator or rewriting number form.
Do not tag borrowing or regrouping steps used to repair a negative fractional result.
Do not tag simplification-only or recombination-only steps when no subtraction is performed in that step.

skills.name: Regroup and simplify
skills.definition: Borrow across whole and fractional parts when needed and express the result in lowest terms, including reduced fraction, mixed-number, or integer form.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when 1 whole is borrowed and converted into fractional units to continue subtraction.
Tag when a fraction result is reduced to lowest terms.
Tag when a zero fraction is simplified away or the result is expressed in proper mixed-number or integer form as part of the post-subtraction adjustment.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag straightforward subtraction steps that require no borrowing and no reduction.
Do not tag initial normalization of whole numbers or improper mixed numbers before subtraction.

decisions.details: Renamed C01 'Equalize fraction units' to S01 'Equalize denominators'
decisions.reasoning: The concept had 3/3 consensus and was retained, but the new name is shorter and more transparent for annotators while preserving the same operation of finding a common denominator and converting to equivalent fractions.

decisions.details: Refined C01 into S01 with clarified exclusion boundary for whole-number rewrites versus denominator equalization
decisions.reasoning: Dossiers include cases where whole numbers are written as 0/d forms; this can be confused with normalization. The refined criteria improve boundary clarity and support consistent tagging.

decisions.details: Renamed C02 'Normalize composite numbers' to S02 'Normalize number form'
decisions.reasoning: The candidate had 3/3 consensus. The revised name is broader and clearer across whole numbers, mixed numbers, and nonstandard mixed numbers without changing the underlying skill.

decisions.details: Refined C02 into S02 to explicitly include decomposition into whole and fractional parts and rewriting whole numbers as n + 0/d
decisions.reasoning: This preserves completeness across items such as FS07, FS09, FS17, and FS19 while keeping the skill distinct from denominator equalization and regrouping.

decisions.details: Kept C03 as S03 'Subtract aligned parts' with minor wording refinement
decisions.reasoning: This skill is independently testable, appears across many items, and is cognitively distinct from preparation steps and post-subtraction adjustment. It is essential for Q-matrix completeness.

decisions.details: Refined C03 into S03 by excluding recombination-only steps and allowing subtraction steps that temporarily produce negative fractional parts
decisions.reasoning: The dossiers show subtraction can occur before regrouping in items like FS10, FS13, FS18, and FS20. This sharper boundary improves annotator agreement and separates subtraction from later repair/simplification.

decisions.details: Kept C04 as S04 'Regroup and simplify'
decisions.reasoning: All experts combined borrowing/regrouping and simplification, and within this item set these operations do not support a cleaner independent split under the exactly-4-skill constraint. Keeping them together preserves consensus and minimality.

decisions.details: Refined C04 into S04 to state that it covers borrowing and post-subtraction reduction to lowest terms, including whole-number or mixed-number expression
decisions.reasoning: This captures dossier evidence such as FS05, FS08, FS10, FS15, and FS18 and clarifies that the skill applies to post-subtraction adjustment rather than initial setup.

summary: All four aligned candidates had full 3/3 expert consensus, so the final consolidation retained the same four-skill structure. The main work was refinement and renaming for clearer annotation boundaries: S01 covers denominator equalization, S02 covers structural rewriting of numbers, S03 covers the actual subtraction once forms are compatible, and S04 covers borrowing and post-subtraction simplification. This preserves completeness, keeps skills distinct and diagnosable, and satisfies the required four-skill codebook.
